newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end lower tracking Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end lower tracking Wall Street.

text.p: Brazil shares continued their downward correction, ending off 1.69 percent on Thursday, again depressed by Dow weakness following warnings by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended down 1,511 points at 87,768 points. Turnover was high at 608.1 million reais ($578.7 million).
On Wednesday, Greenspan spooked world markets by raising questions about the sustainability of Wall Street's rise and suggesting that a hike in U.S. rates could be needed.
Brokers said the market is likely to remain weak Friday as Telebras preferred shares could fall to as low as 98 reais, considered by technical analysts as the stock's resistance level.

Telebras preferred stock fell 1.93 percent to close at 101.60 reais. Power utility Eletrobras closed at 472 reais, off 0.84 percent. Oil state firm Petrobras preferred stock ended down 1.85 percent to close at 212 reais.
